summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, diastolic heart failure, alcoholic cirrhosis, and prior right knee infection was admitted for revision total knee replacement. The surgery was performed successfully after removal of an antibiotic spacer. Postoperatively, she received two packed red blood cell transfusions for acute blood loss anemia and was managed with IV antibiotics, pain control, and DVT prophylaxis with Lovenox. Her wound healed well with no signs of infection, and labs showed improvement in hemoglobin. She was transitioned to oral medications, participated in physical therapy, and was discharged to a rehabilitation facility with instructions for anticoagulation, wound care, and follow-up. No active infection was found in intraoperative cultures.
